drhp.business: INDO SMC Limited designs and manufactures enclosure boxes for energy meters, HTCT/HTPT/LTCT transformers, LT/HT distribution boxes and panels, FRP grating, junction boxes, feeder pillars and other power distribution and circuit-protection switchgear. The business is organised into three divisions: sheet moulding compound (SMC enclosure boxes, SMC sheet/chequered plates), fiberglass reinforced plastic (grating, pultrusion) and electrical components (CT/PTs, feeder pillars), serving DISCOMs, government distribution schemes and private industrial/power-sector clients.
drhp.end_markets: DISCOMs and power distribution utilities|Government Smart Meter National Programme (SMNP)|Government Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS)|Private-sector power and transformer sector clients|Industrial and infrastructure clients
drhp.expansion: Company undertook capital expenditure and expanded installed capacities across all segments in Fiscal 2025 versus Fiscal 2024, with capacity up 117.20% in the SMC segment and 74.71% in the FRP segment. During FY2025 it also established a new LTCT and CT/PT manufacturing unit at Nashik, Maharashtra, and introduced new products (FRP gratings, CT/PT units) based on confirmed business leads from power and transformer sector clients. The company currently operates four manufacturing facilities located across Gujarat, Maharashtra and Rajasthan.

overview.business_model: Per the Memorandum of Association, the company manufactures, supplies and deals in electrical apparatus for switching or protecting electrical circuits (switches, relays, fuses, surge suppressors, plugs, sockets, lamp-holders, connectors, junction boxes, optical-fibre connectors). Following the August 2025 object amendment, the objects also cover: manufacturing/trading of Fibre Glass Reinforced Polymer (FRP) products (FRP pultruded products, FRP moulded gratings, FRP rods) including design, prototyping, manufacturing, logistics, installation and after-sales service; technical consultancy/advisory services in Sheet Molding Compound (SMC) and FRP composite materials (formulation, process optimisation, R&D, feasibility studies) including for power-sector infrastructure such as transformers, solar and EV stations/batteries; manufacturing/trading of Current Transformers (CTs), Potential Transformers (PTs), combined CT-PT units and other electrical measuring/metering instruments; and manufacture/dealing in tarpaulins, synthetic and geo-membrane products.

genesis.founding_story: Initial subscribers to the Memorandum of Association were Mr. Nitin Jasavantbhai Patel, Mr. Pranay Girishkumar Sonawala, Mr. Chaitanya Patel and Mr. Neel Niteshbhai Shah (2,500 equity shares each, 10,000 shares total), with the stated aim of manufacturing and supplying electrical apparatus for switching/protecting electrical circuits. The company was converted to a public limited company and renamed 'Indo SMC Limited' pursuant to a special resolution of shareholders dated June 18, 2024. Current promoters are Mr. Nitin Jasavantbhai Patel, Mrs. Riktaben Sonawala, Mr. Chaitanya Patel, Mr. Neel Niteshbhai Shah and Mr. Rachit Jain.

overview.one_liner: Indo SMC Limited is an Ahmedabad-based manufacturer originally incorporated to make electrical switching/protection apparatus, with its Memorandum of Association object clause expanded (August 2025) to also cover FRP products, SMC/FRP technical consultancy, CT/PT transformers and tarpaulin/geomembrane products.

verdict_pointers: Two bonus issues (6:1 in August 2024 and 2:1 in December 2024) plus two preferential/private-placement allotments (March 2024, September 2024) occurred within roughly a year of this DRHP filing -- a concentrated near-IPO capital build-up worth cross-checking against the 'capital_history' entries.
Promoter and promoter group hold 82.32% pre-issue with no shares shown as pledged or otherwise encumbered per the shareholding pattern table.

The main object clause was amended on August 30, 2025 -- shortly before this filing -- expanding scope from the original electrical switching/protection apparatus business to also include FRP products, SMC/FRP technical consultancy, CT/PT transformers and tarpaulins/geomembrane products; see 'Our Business' for the company's actual current segment mix versus this broadened object clause.

internal_operational.detail: Company vulnerable to fluctuating global/Indian raw material prices; no long-term supply agreements, purchases on spot-market basis.
internal_operational.evidence: Raw material consumption was 82.12% of revenue for period ended Sep 30, 2025, 71.32% FY2025, 88.56% FY2024, and 106.36% FY2023 of revenue from operations.
internal_operational.title: Raw material price increase / high raw material dependency

internal_operational.detail: Project work orders awarded via competitive bidding and qualification criteria; no assurance bids will be accepted or projects tendered on announced timelines.
internal_operational.evidence: Company bids for selective government and private projects; bid preparation involves considerable time and resources with no assurance of qualification or acceptance.
internal_operational.title: Revenue largely dependent on competitive bidding process

internal_operational.detail: Large portion of raw materials procured from a few key suppliers without long-term supply contracts; discontinuation or delay could hamper production.
internal_operational.evidence: Purchases from top ten suppliers were Rs. 8,531.49 Lakhs (period ended Sep 30, 2025), Rs. 3,178.50 Lakhs (FY2025), Rs. 1,620.93 Lakhs (FY2024) and Rs. 572.64 Lakhs (FY2023), representing 92.31%, 32.14%, 65.29% and 73.80% respectively of total raw material consumed.
internal_operational.title: Dependence on few key raw material suppliers

internal_operational.detail: Capacity utilization has fluctuated across plants; adequate utilization of expanded capacities depends on demand, regulatory approvals and personnel; company is registering with additional state electricity boards (Karnataka, MP, UP) to raise utilization.
internal_operational.evidence: SMC Electrical Enclosures & Sheets utilization: 66.42% FY2022-23, 73.42% FY2023-24, 56.48% FY2024-25, 33.03% FY2025-26 (till Sep 30, 2025, not annualized). FRP Gratings & Pultruded Sections: 63.93%, 69.97%, 46.86%, 38.77% respectively. Combined total utilization: 65.72%, 72.25%, 53.67%, 34.70%. Nashik unit Low Tension Current Transformer utilization: 92.86% FY2024-25 vs 36.11% FY2025-26 (till Sep 30, 2025).
internal_operational.title: Under-utilization of manufacturing capacities / expansion utilization risk

internal_operational.detail: No long-term or exclusive arrangements with customers; orders on purchase-order basis without fixed-volume commitment; customers may cancel orders at short notice.
internal_operational.evidence: Top 10 customers represented 82.94% of revenue (Rs. 9,334.02 Lakhs, period ended Sep 30, 2025), 65.75% (Rs. 9,118.27 Lakhs, FY2025), 75.92% (Rs. 2,128.29 Lakhs, FY2024) and 87.97% (Rs. 641.80 Lakhs, FY2023). Customer 1 alone was 65.12% of revenue (Rs. 7,328.22 Lakhs) in the period ended Sep 30, 2025.
internal_operational.title: Customer concentration; no long-term customer arrangements

internal_operational.detail: Manufacturing activities carry hazards including explosions, fires, mechanical failures, natural disasters and hazardous substance discharge.
internal_operational.evidence: Company has not encountered fatalities or employee injuries in the last three Fiscals and current Fiscal until date of RHP.
internal_operational.title: Manufacturing hazards - risk of injury to people or property

strategy_growth.detail: Company has received third-party quotations but has not placed orders for proposed machinery; quotations valid for limited periods and subject to revision, risking cost/time overruns.
strategy_growth.evidence: Machinery proposed to be purchased from Net Proceeds amounts to approximately Rs. 2,570.67 Lakhs.
strategy_growth.title: Yet to place orders for expansion machinery (Ghiloth Rajasthan, Ahmedabad and Nashik units)

strategy_growth.detail: Expansion at Ghiloth (Rajasthan), Nashik (Maharashtra) and Ahmedabad (Gujarat) requires substantial capex dependent on Net Proceeds financing and performance of external agencies for construction, installation and commissioning.
strategy_growth.evidence: Completion dependent on ability to arrange finance through Net Proceeds or otherwise per RHP disclosure.
strategy_growth.title: Delays/cost overruns risk in proposed manufacturing expansion

strategy_growth.detail: Substantial revenue dependence on economic/industrial conditions in these two states limits diversification against regional risks.
strategy_growth.evidence: Approximately 90.20% of total revenue for the period ended September 30, 2025 was generated from customers located within Gujarat and Maharashtra.
strategy_growth.title: Significant geographical revenue concentration in Gujarat and Maharashtra

strategy_growth.detail: Rapid historical growth requires continued upgrades to controls, policies, procedures and management systems; failure to manage growth could adversely affect operations.
strategy_growth.evidence: Revenue from operations grew from Rs. 729.55 Lakhs in Fiscal 2023 to Rs. 13,869.25 Lakhs in Fiscal 2025 (CAGR 336.01% over 3 years); PAT grew from Rs. 45.52 Lakhs in Fiscal 2023 to Rs. 1,544.04 Lakhs in Fiscal 2025 (CAGR 482.42% over 3 years).
strategy_growth.title: Risk of failure to manage rapid business growth

strategy_growth.detail: Business is vulnerable to regional economic conditions, demographic shifts, natural disasters, cyber-attacks, and political/social unrest.
strategy_growth.evidence: Company describes exposure to region-specific natural disasters, telecommunications failures, cyber-attacks, riots and political unrest per RHP.
strategy_growth.title: Industry sensitivity to general economic downturn

strategy_growth.detail: Faces competition from numerous unorganized players as well as established players with greater financial/technical/marketing resources.
strategy_growth.evidence: Low entry barriers cited as facilitating potential new competitor entry per RHP disclosure.
strategy_growth.title: Competitive, fragmented industry with low entry barriers

concerns_observed: Operating cash flow was negative in every reported period (CFO Rs -290.14 FY23, -577.84 FY24, -1,370.34 FY25, -704.52 H1FY26 lakhs); growth has been funded by financing inflows (CFF positive each year) rather than internally generated cash.

Extreme customer concentration: Customer 1 alone was 65.12% of revenue (Rs 7,328.22 lakhs) in H1FY26; top-5 customers 78.08% and top-10 82.94% of H1FY26 revenue, with no long-term or exclusive customer contracts (purchase-order basis).

Single-product dependence emerging: Bus Duct went from 0% of revenue (FY23-FY24) to 65.12% in H1FY26 while the historical mainstay SMC Box fell from 87.51% (FY23) to 21.86% (H1FY26); the H1FY26 revenue surge and the Customer-1 share appear linked to one product line.
Geographic concentration: approximately 90.20% of H1FY26 revenue came from Gujarat and Maharashtra combined.

Supplier concentration with no long-term supply agreements: top-10 suppliers were 92.31% of raw material consumed in H1FY26; raw-material cost was 106.36% of revenue in FY23 and 82.12% in H1FY26, leaving margins exposed to spot-price moves.

100% of the Rs 2,570.67-lakh capex machinery (all 25 line items) is backed only by vendor quotations dated Aug-Dec 2025 (validity 60 days to 6 months); no purchase orders have been placed, creating cost/time-overrun exposure.

Capacity utilisation is falling while the company expands: combined SMC+FRP utilisation declined 72.25% (FY24) to 53.67% (FY25) to 34.70% (H1FY26 part-year), and Nashik LTCT utilisation fell from 92.86% (FY25) to 36.11% (H1FY26).

Governance and statutory-compliance gaps: Managing Director also serves as CFO; only 2 of 6 directors are independent; 19 delayed ROC e-form filings rectified with additional fees; a pending adjudication over Ind AS-format financials (FY22-FY24); factory-license/CTE-CTO address discrepancy under rectification; and Nashik Fire NOC still pending.

parameter_scores.basis: Strong reported growth and 15-18% EBITDA margins, but operating cash flow negative all four periods (CFO -704.52 lakhs H1FY26, -1,370.34 lakhs FY25) with receivables of Rs 5,476.45 lakhs and inventory of Rs 4,730.02 lakhs at Sep-30-2025 against H1 revenue of Rs 11,254.11 lakhs; raw material was 106.36% of revenue in FY23.

Company incorporated only Sept-2021; MD (Neel Shah) doubles as CFO; only 2 of 6 directors independent; one executive director is Matric-pass; 19 delayed statutory e-form filings, pending Ind AS-format adjudication (Form GNL-1, Sept-2025), and manufacturing/storage plots leased from promoters and a promoter-group company.

Customer 1 = 65.12% of H1FY26 revenue and top-10 = 82.94%; ~90.20% of revenue from Gujarat+Maharashtra; top-10 suppliers = 92.31% of RM consumed; single product (Bus Duct) = 65.12% of revenue; borrowings from only two lenders (HDFC Bank and Standard Chartered).

All Rs 2,570.67-lakh capex machinery backed only by quotations, no orders placed (100% of capex); utilisation declining to 34.70% combined while expanding; main object clause broadened only Aug-2025 into FRP/CT-PT/tarpaulin verticals that contribute minimal revenue to date.

No OFS (all fresh capital) is positive, but two bonus issues (6:1 Aug-2024, 2:1 Dec-2024) plus preferential placements occurred within ~18 months of filing; promoter average acquisition cost is Rs 0.48/share for four promoters and Rs 2.38/share for the fifth versus the issue price; total debt Rs 4,935.16 lakhs vs net worth Rs 4,714.11 lakhs (H1FY26).

red_flags: Negative operating cash flow in all four reported periods (CFO -290.14, -577.84, -1,370.34, -704.52 lakhs) despite a 336% three-year revenue CAGR, indicating growth is not converting to operating cash.
Single-customer dependence at 65.12% of H1FY26 revenue (Rs 7,328.22 lakhs) with no long-term contract, concurrent with a single product (Bus Duct) at 65.12% of revenue.
Two bonus issues (6:1 and 2:1) plus preferential placements within ~18 months before filing, with promoter average acquisition cost of Rs 0.48/share (four promoters) versus the issue price.
strengths_observed: Rapid top-line and earnings scale-up: revenue rose from Rs 729.55 lakhs (FY23) to Rs 13,869.25 lakhs (FY25) with H1FY26 already at Rs 11,254.11 lakhs; PAT rose from Rs 45.52 lakhs (FY23) to Rs 1,544.09 lakhs (FY25) (stated revenue CAGR 336.01% and PAT CAGR 482.42% over three years).
Double-digit EBITDA margins sustained through the scale change (15.83% FY23, 18.12% FY24, 16.45% FY25, 15.27% H1FY26) with PAT margins of ~10-11% in three of four periods.
High headline return ratios (ROCE 20.71% FY24, 31.39% FY25; ROE 86.24% FY24, 74.45% FY25), albeit computed on a small and rapidly expanding equity base.

Issue is entirely fresh capital with no Offer-for-Sale component: 61,71,000 shares directed to plant-and-machinery capex (Rs 2,570.67 lakhs) and working capital (Rs 5,200 lakhs); promoters are not monetising holdings.
No promoter/promoter-group shares shown as pledged or encumbered; promoter and promoter group hold 82.32% pre-issue.

Product platform spans three divisions (SMC enclosures/sheets, FRP gratings/pultrusion, electrical components/CT-PT) across three manufacturing locations (Ahmedabad, Nashik, Ghiloth) with ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015 and IS:13410/IS:14772 compliance and in-house multi-stage testing laboratories.
Low absolute litigation exposure: total quantified proceedings Rs 55.87 lakhs (~1.19% of net worth), of which only Rs 0.91 lakhs relates to the Company itself and Rs 54.96 lakhs to Promoters.

sk.overview: The Sheet Molding Compound (SMC) market comprises composite materials made from a combination of resin, filler, and chopped fibers, commonly used in automotive, construction, and electrical applications. SMC offers advantages such as lightweight properties, high strength, corrosion resistance, and design flexibility, making it a preferred alternative to metals in many industrial sectors, with growing adoption in electric vehicle components, renewable energy infrastructure, and industrial equipment.
